title: Determination of Forward and Futures Prices: Part 1
prerequisites: Continuous compounding and discounting A = P * e^(rT)
Basic concepts of short selling and security borrowing
Term structure of interest rates from Chapter 4
learningOutcomes: Classify assets into investment versus consumption assets and explain arbitrage pricing boundaries.
Calculate theoretical forward prices for no-income assets using F_0 = S_0 * e^(rT).
Construct cash-and-carry and reverse cash-and-carry arbitrage portfolios when market prices diverge.
Adjust forward prices for known discrete cash dividends: F_0 = (S_0 - I) * e^(rT).
Model continuous dividend yields using F_0 = S_0 * e^((r - q)*T) and define cost of carry.
Analyze the Kidder Peabody scandal to explain how discounting timing errors generate phantom accounting profits.

sections.title: Asset Typology & Short Selling Mechanics
sections.pedagogicalObjective: Establish the distinction between investment and consumption assets and detail short selling obligations.
keyPoints: Investment assets allow two-way arbitrage; consumption assets only establish upper bounds.
Short sellers must pay all dividends to lenders and face repo special borrowing costs.
Short squeezes force premature closeout when borrow supply dries up.

sections.title: No-Arbitrage Forward Pricing: No Income Assets
sections.pedagogicalObjective: Derive F_0 = S_0 * e^(rT) and prove cash-and-carry replication.
keyPoints: Theoretical forward price equals spot price compounded at the risk-free rate.
F_0 > S_0 * e^(rT) triggers cash-and-carry (borrow cash, buy spot, short forward).
F_0 < S_0 * e^(rT) triggers reverse cash-and-carry (short spot, invest cash, long forward).

sections.title: Forward Pricing with Known Income & Dividends
sections.pedagogicalObjective: Formulate forward pricing adjustments for discrete cash coupons and continuous dividend yields.
keyPoints: Discrete cash dividends reduce forward price: F_0 = (S_0 - I) * e^(rT).
Continuous dividend yield q offsets financing cost: F_0 = S_0 * e^((r - q)*T).
Cost of carry c = r - q; if q > r, forward trades at a discount to spot.

sections.title: Kidder Peabody's $350M Phantom Forward STRIPs
sections.pedagogicalObjective: Dissect Snapshot 5.1 to show how failing to discount forward commitments creates fictitious trading profits.
keyPoints: Trader Joseph Jett exploited accounting software that credited future stripped bond values today without discounting.
Created $350M in phantom accounting profits while losing $210M in actual trading.
Destroyed Kidder Peabody and led to its acquisition by PaineWebber.

misconceptions.misconception: The forward price of an asset represents the market's expected future spot price.
misconceptions.authorRebuttal: Forward price is purely determined by the cost of financing spot storage (F_0 = S_0 * e^(rT)) to prevent arbitrage, irrespective of whether investors expect prices to rise or fall.

misconceptions.misconception: Dividends increase the forward price because the asset generates cash flow.
misconceptions.authorRebuttal: Dividends are collected by the spot holder, not the forward buyer. Therefore, dividends reduce the forward price: F_0 = (S_0 - I) * e^(rT).

misconceptions.misconception: Short sellers can hold short positions indefinitely at zero extra cost.
misconceptions.authorRebuttal: Short sellers face stock borrowing fees, repo specials, and risk of forced buy-ins during short squeezes.

activeRecallQuiz.scenario: A non-dividend-paying stock trades at $50. The continuous risk-free interest rate is 6% per annum for all maturities. An investor wants to determine the 6-month theoretical forward price.
activeRecallQuiz.question: What is the theoretical 6-month forward price of the stock?

coreTakeaways: Investment assets obey strict two-way no-arbitrage bounds; consumption assets only obey upper bounds.
No-income forward price F_0 = S_0 * e^(rT) reflects the pure cost of carrying the spot asset.
Known discrete cash dividends reduce forward price to F_0 = (S_0 - I) * e^(rT).
Continuous dividend yields reduce carry cost: F_0 = S_0 * e^((r - q)*T).
Kidder Peabody collapsed because accounting software failed to discount forward delivery commitments.
